purpose: Explain the four unsupported atoms in the strongest legacy 9/13 teacher control without changing the frozen LOCAL_FIRST_ALLOCATION_FALLBACK_HYBRID_V1 design or inspecting the sealed acceptance benchmark.

scope.strongest_legacy_control_result: 9/13 supported atoms with all 7/7 frozen controls plus e1.a and e6.a

diagnostic_semantics.oracle_query_diagnostic: One teacher-derived but answer-free evidence query is issued separately for each atom. Each retriever gets up to top-12 propositions for that atom-specific query. A 13/13 score means every atom's required source anchors appear within its own top-12 list; it does NOT mean a single 12- or 24-proposition final evidence set contains all 13 atoms, and it does NOT test automatic discovery of which questions to ask.
diagnostic_semantics.interpretation: The ranking/retrieval substrate has sufficient capacity under precise information needs. The gap between oracle performance and automatic 9/13 performance is primarily about automatic intent/obligation coverage, evidence allocation/fusion, and final evidence-set selection rather than missing source evidence or an intrinsically incapable retriever.

atoms.normalized_form: The proposed framework trains a classifier using source-domain device labels.
atoms.exact_support_text_summary: The base encoder is used as a feature extractor and the classifier is trained from extracted features plus device labels from the source domain only.
atoms.oracle_query: How is the classifier trained after representation learning, and which domain provides the device labels?
automatic_intent_evidence: Wave 7A source-aware diagnostic explicitly reports that no separate source-label classifier-training intent was generated.
Author-anchored generation asks how the base encoder is used in the subsequent training stage, but does not atomically ask which domain provides device labels.
The exact support proposition page:p2:s34 is absent from every Wave 7A.3 automatic merged top-24 arm.

A semantically equivalent page:p4:s15 proposition about source-domain device labels appears in the deterministic BGE automatic top-24, showing that the exact-page anchor evaluator can undercount semantically valid support in some arms; it is not present in the strongest 9/13 composed/rescued set.
atoms.implication: Do not scale the ranker. The evidence is easy to retrieve once an atomic source-label training obligation exists. A future bounded design should test explicit atomic method-stage obligation coverage and source-fidelity evaluation.

atoms.normalized_form: The proposed framework tests on target-domain data.
atoms.exact_support_text_summary: The trained base encoder and classifier are applied to target data during testing.
atoms.oracle_query: Which domain's data is used during the testing stage?
automatic_intent_evidence: Wave 7A source-aware diagnostic explicitly reports that no separate target-domain testing intent was generated.
Automatic merged sets contain broad stage/domain-shift propositions, but the exact target-testing proposition page:p2:s35 is absent from all Wave 7A.3 automatic top-24 arms.
The strongest 9/13 composed/rescued set also omits page:p2:s35.
atoms.implication: This is the cleanest evidence that compound method descriptions need decomposition by lifecycle stage. The existing retrievers find the atom at rank 1-3 under a precise answer-free query.

atoms.normalized_form: The wireless testbed sampled frames with an Ettus USRP B210 at 45 MSps.
atoms.exact_support_text_summary: Wireless frames are sampled/stored as IQ by an Ettus USRP B210 at 45 MSps.
atoms.oracle_query: What receiver hardware and sampling rate are used to capture the wireless frames?
automatic_intent_evidence: Source-aware automatic generation does cover acquisition, but splits the need into a hardware/protocol question and a sampling-rate/center-frequency question rather than a single joint hardware+rate obligation.
Under the source-aware BGE-M3 hybrid arm, page:p2:s17 is selected at fusion rank 13 and e3.c is supported.
Under the stronger source-aware BM25 control, page:p2:s17 is absent and e3.c is not supported.
The strongest 9/13 composed/rescued set omits page:p2:s17.
atoms.implication: This is not a missing-intent problem in the same sense as e1.b/e1.c. The system asks about acquisition, but splitting coupled attributes plus the selected fusion path loses the joint evidence. A future design should preserve coupled acquisition obligations or join shallow evidence across related intents rather than globally swap retrievers.

atoms.normalized_form: The authors identify consistently misclassified devices as an area for further research.
atoms.exact_support_text_summary: Certain devices are consistently misclassified and the authors plan to investigate the cause.
atoms.oracle_query: What future work do the authors identify for devices that are consistently misclassified?
automatic_intent_evidence: Wave 7A source-aware generation explicitly failed to create a separate persistent-misclassification future-work intent.
Author-anchored generation does create a misclassification-cause question.
Its BM25 merged top-24 selects page:p6:s09 at rank 18: Device 10 is consistently mistaken for Device 5 with high probability, warranting further investigation.
The frozen exact-anchor evaluator still reports e6.c unsupported because it requires the exact page:p6:s15 wording; page:p6:s15 itself is absent.
The strongest 9/13 composed/rescued set contains neither page:p6:s15 nor page:p6:s09.
atoms.implication: Precise retrieval is trivial under the oracle query. The source-aware branch needs an atomic misclassification/failure-mode obligation, while evaluation should recognize source-faithful paraphrastic evidence instead of depending only on one exact anchor wording.

primary_failure_families: legacy exact-page/exact-anchor evaluator brittleness on repeated or paraphrastic source evidence
synthesis.interpretation: The four residuals should not be accepted as unexplained losses. Existing development evidence says they are mostly tractable architecture/evaluation problems, not irreducible retrieval failures.

recommended_next_boundary.timing: After the already-frozen LOCAL_FIRST_ALLOCATION_FALLBACK_HYBRID_V1 receives its genuine result and independent post-result review; do not change that hybrid mid-experiment.
recommended_next_boundary.objective: Using only the legacy development paper and frozen source/proposition substrate, test whether an explicit teacher-blind atomic-obligation coverage layer can expose e1.b/e1.c/e6.c and preserve the joint acquisition fact e3.c without sacrificing established controls. Separately run a source-fidelity audit of repeated/paraphrastic support so the legacy 13-atom score does not mistake valid evidence for a miss.
prohibited: changing the currently frozen hybrid before its result
new model-family scaling merely to chase 13/13
recommended_next_boundary.acceptance_freeze_rule: Do not declare ACCEPTANCE_CANDIDATE_FROZEN while these four remain merely unexplained. Before freeze, either close the tractable residual mechanism with bounded development evidence or demonstrate that the final completeness/fallback controller reliably refuses local completion when analogous CORE obligations are missing.
